I need to find the characteristic polynomial of the matrix $A = \begin{pmatrix} -4 & -13 & 10 \\ -9 & 10 & 4 \\ 12 & -5 & -14 \end{pmatrix}$.

The characteristic polynomial is $\det(A - \lambda I)$.

$$A - \lambda I = \begin{pmatrix} -4-\lambda & -13 & 10 \\ -9 & 10-\lambda & 4 \\ 12 & -5 & -14-\lambda \end{pmatrix}$$

I'll compute the determinant by expanding along the first row:

$$\det(A - \lambda I) = (-4-\lambda)\begin{vmatrix} 10-\lambda & 4 \\ -5 & -14-\lambda \end{vmatrix} + 13\begin{vmatrix} -9 & 4 \\ 12 & -14-\lambda \end{vmatrix} + 10\begin{vmatrix} -9 & 10-\lambda \\ 12 & -5 \end{vmatrix}$$

**First minor:**
$$\begin{vmatrix} 10-\lambda & 4 \\ -5 & -14-\lambda \end{vmatrix} = (10-\lambda)(-14-\lambda) - 4(-5)$$
$$= -140 - 10\lambda + 14\lambda + \lambda^2 + 20 = \lambda^2 + 4\lambda - 120$$

**Second minor:**
$$\begin{vmatrix} -9 & 4 \\ 12 & -14-\lambda \end{vmatrix} = -9(-14-\lambda) - 4(12)$$
$$= 126 + 9\lambda - 48 = 9\lambda + 78$$

**Third minor:**
$$\begin{vmatrix} -9 & 10-\lambda \\ 12 & -5 \end{vmatrix} = -9(-5) - (10-\lambda)(12)$$
$$= 45 - 120 + 12\lambda = 12\lambda - 75$$

Now substituting back:
$$\det(A - \lambda I) = (-4-\lambda)(\lambda^2 + 4\lambda - 120) + 13(9\lambda + 78) + 10(12\lambda - 75)$$

**Expanding the first term:**
$$(-4-\lambda)(\lambda^2 + 4\lambda - 120) = -4\lambda^2 - 16\lambda + 480 - \lambda^3 - 4\lambda^2 + 120\lambda$$
$$= -\lambda^3 - 8\lambda^2 + 104\lambda + 480$$

**Expanding the second term:**
$$13(9\lambda + 78) = 117\lambda + 1014$$

**Expanding the third term:**
$$10(12\lambda - 75) = 120\lambda - 750$$

**Combining all terms:**
$$\det(A - \lambda I) = -\lambda^3 - 8\lambda^2 + 104\lambda + 480 + 117\lambda + 1014 + 120\lambda - 750$$
$$= -\lambda^3 - 8\lambda^2 + (104 + 117 + 120)\lambda + (480 + 1014 - 750)$$
$$= -\lambda^3 - 8\lambda^2 + 341\lambda + 744$$

Therefore, the characteristic polynomial is:

$$\boxed{-\lambda^3 - 8\lambda^2 + 341\lambda + 744}$$
